newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call quiet, gilts end firm in two-way trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call quiet, gilts end firm in two-way trade.

text.p: Indian call money was largely inactive on Friday while securities ended slightly up after volatile trade, dealers said.
Call money ended at 0.1-0.5 percent against opening quotes of 0.75-1.25 percent.
Dealers said there was little trade in call money on Friday, as it is the fortnightly reporting day for banks.
Three-day money ended at 3.74-4.25 percent after opening at 4.0-4.5 percent, they said.
"Given today's rates for three-day money, call should open around 6.0 percent tomorrow," said a foreign bank dealer.
Other dealers said the light volumes traded in three-day money made it difficult to forecast Saturday's rates.
Governemnt securities ended with slight increases but trade was volatile with two-way movement in prices, dealers said.

"Prices moved up in the opening session, fell mid-way and moved up again towards close," said a dealer. "With quite a few traders funding their securities trade thorugh call money, a lot depends on how call opens tomorrow."

The 11.83 percent 2003 government stock rose to 102.90 rupees from its previous close of 102.75 rupees, while the 12.59 percent 2004 ended at 105.88 rupees, off the morning's high of 105.90 but up from Thursday's 105.78 rupees.
The 10.85 percent 2001 improved to 100.85 rupees from 100.77 rupees.
October-maturity treasury bills yielded 6.45 percent against Thursday's 6.35 percent, dealers said.
A certificate of deposit maturing in mid-August was traded at a yield of 7.0 percent.
